en: The 10-18 analysis found #1342 refreshes /ui/idd only after local executions; a change on another peer or from CI reaches the page only by polling. 5a's I2981 (in flight, no record yet) pushes board and journal changes over one WebSocket for the blackboard; this issue makes every page that reads mesh-derived state follow it. I3194 (latency) duplicated I3140 (prismatic-lumen) and is dropped in favour of it. It extends milestone everything-is-followed-in-one-stream. Proposed in ADR 0201 (The persistent runtime is the authority; every operator surface, Lumen included, is a client of it); ADR 0216 (Every live surface follows one channel with named follow streams, and nothing polls where a stream exists) (proposed; it carries no authority until the owner accepts it). en: The runtime keeps one bit saying whether a shared server decided anything (activated, or declined with a reason); the doctor's `runtime` check reads the server's decision when the bit is set and reports an absence when it is not, and `majordomus mesh doctor` asks the running server for its report so that the verdict is the server's. It does not make the mesh reach anybody, and hubs are started by hand.

Knihovna hooků z této zprávy vykreslí řádek briefingu a sama žádný požadavek neposílá. apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mesh.rs dokazuje tři verdikty na skutečném serveru; případ dokazuje odpovědi briefingu a návratový kód přes startovací událost poskytovatele a čte potvrzenou deklaraci tohoto repozitáře (ADR 0059). en: The takeover itself is correct, the stale-executable guard doing its job; what was unowned was the aftermath. The superseded process kept its socket, its peer board and its generation of the layer, and answered GET / with the same name and repository_id as the leaseholder, so every liveness test in the system passed on it. Measured on 2026-09-10 - two servers of one checkout, one lease, and a session whose environment carried the older address reading a board with one peer where the shared board had two. GET / now carries leaseholder (lease::LEASEHOLDER_KEY, read by lease::probe, so writer and reader cannot drift), a new initialize is refused 409 lease_lost naming the launcher, and health.report's server check warns that this process is not the server it describes. A server too old to answer the question is accepted by the probe on purpose - refusing it would take over a live server, which is how one checkout comes to have two. The doctrine is project.shared-server-resilience.
cs: Samotné převzetí je správné, hlídač zastaralého spustitelného souboru udělal svou práci; bez vlastníka zůstaly jeho důsledky. Vystřídaný proces si ponechal svůj socket, svou nástěnku peerů i svou generaci vrstvy a na GET / odpovídal stejným name a repository_id jako držitel leasu, takže na něm prošel každý test živosti v systému. Změřeno 2026-09-10 - dva servery jednoho checkoutu, jeden lease a relace, jejíž prostředí nesla starší adresu a četla nástěnku s jedním peerem, zatímco sdílená nástěnka měla dva. GET / nyní nese leaseholder (lease::LEASEHOLDER_KEY, čte ho lease::probe, takže zapisovatel a čtenář se nemohou rozejít), nový initialize je odmítnut s 409 lease_lost a jménem launcheru a kontrola serveru v health.report varuje, že tento proces není serverem, který popisuje. Server příliš starý na to, aby na otázku odpověděl, probe záměrně přijme - jeho odmítnutí by převzalo živý server, a tak se stane, že jeden checkout má servery dva. Doktrína je project.shared-server-resilience.

Every finding names the samples it rests on (<t4/>), the runner and its 1-minute load average at the start and end of the run: on 2026-10-08 one cold sample of <t5/> read 9 -> 23 ms on a saturated runner and failed a change that ran none of the measured code. en: <t1>One episode per provider session, not one per worktree.</t1> Two windows of the same provider open on one checkout are two workers. Folding them into one record stamped one worker's ledger lines with the other's id and let either window's end event close the episode for both; measured in this repository on 2026-09-09, seven concurrent sessions produced one record between them. So an open episode is a file of its own, <t2/>, keyed by the provider session that opened it. <t3/> keeps <t4>your</t4> episode — which is why it exists: the start event fires again on a resume and on a compaction — and gives a different provider session an episode of its own. <t5/> closes that episode and no other, which is what a provider's end event passes. An episode nobody named is keyed <t6/>, and there is at most one of those: a provider that sends no session identity is indistinguishable from a person at a terminal, and inventing a distinction there would multiply episodes nobody can close. A hand-opened episode needs no provider anywhere and behaves exactly as before.
cs: <t1>Jedna epizoda na relaci poskytovatele, ne jedna na worktree.</t1> Dvě okna téhož poskytovatele otevřená na jednom checkoutu jsou dva pracovníci. Jejich sloučení do jednoho záznamu označilo řádky knihy jednoho pracovníka id druhého a nechalo koncovou událost kteréhokoli okna zavřít epizodu pro oba; změřeno v tomto repozitáři 2026-09-09, sedm souběžných relací mezi sebou vyprodukovalo jeden záznam. Otevřená epizoda je proto vlastní soubor, <t2/>, klíčovaný relací poskytovatele, která ji otevřela. <t3/> ponechává <t4>vaši</t4> epizodu — proto existuje: startovní událost se spouští znovu při obnovení a při kompakci — a jiné relaci poskytovatele dává vlastní epizodu. <t5/> zavře tuto epizodu a žádnou jinou, což je to, co předává koncová událost poskytovatele. Epizoda, kterou nikdo nepojmenoval, je klíčována <t6/> a je nejvýše jedna: poskytovatel, který neposílá identitu relace, je nerozlišitelný od člověka u terminálu a vymýšlet tam rozdíl by množilo epizody, které nikdo nezavře. Ručně otevřená epizoda nepotřebuje nikde žádného poskytovatele a chová se přesně jako dřív.

en: A native surface `ui` is mounted at /ui (topology, binding, router; Feature::Ui) and served by the shared server beside the Cockpit, which it refers to only as the technical view of a source. Its frame follows the owner's references: a sidebar of screens with the kit's icons (compiled from site/data/kit/icons.toml by majordomus generate) and a version card read from distribution.releases, a top bar with the search, the time the screen was read and the other surfaces, and a menu that opens without JavaScript. Seven screens — Dashboard, Roadmap, Issues & PRs, Mesh, CI/CD & Releases, Evidence, Governance — each a hero band with KPI tiles and a grid of panels, compose only capability answers asked at once. Every panel names its sources with the API route, CLI command and MCP tool capabilities.describe declares. Tiles, panels and rows lead to the screen holding the whole. Milestone dependencies are drawn as a graph with the vendored Cytoscape over a table fallback. Donuts, meters and timelines are drawn server-side from the counts they list, and a missing value reads none, unknown or not answered, never zero. The pull-request queue is the panel /ui/panels/pull-requests, pulled in after paint. A visible screen is read again every minute and says when. ui-integrity and the ADR 0012 index check cover src/ui (cases 389 and 547), and the CI class ui selects the asset check whenever share/ui or src/ui changes. Not done here: the majordomus ui command (I2231, to be amended), and the Command, Capabilities, Deployments, Documentation and Settings screens.
